why: A design exercise for the basic singly linked list: get, add at head, add at tail, add before index and delete at index all reduce to 'walk to the node before position i, then relink', made uniform by a dummy head node.
hints: Keep a size counter so you can reject invalid indices without walking the list.
A dummy node in front of the real head means 'insert at 0' and 'delete index 0' are the same code as any other index: walk i steps from the dummy to the predecessor.
Insert: p.next = Node(val, p.next). Delete: p.next = p.next.next. Each operation is O(index), at most O(n), fine for 1000 operations.
pitfalls: Add-at with a negative index means the head; index == length appends; index > length does nothing.
Delete and get need 0 <= index < length; a negative index is invalid for them.
Every non-get operation returns 0, even when it was ignored.
